topics.topic: Exact configuration schema: environment-variable names, settings fields and types, and their mappings
questions: What exact environment-variable name corresponds to each listed configuration item, including each of the four service tokens?
What are the settings object's exact field names and types, and how does each environment variable map to them?
What is the exact environment-variable name for every listed item, especially each service token, so Registry can decide whether a name names an item or is an ignored misspelling?
What is the settings model or authority module, and what are the exact field names and types through which each item reaches generated Registry code?
Replace the generic reference to unnamed settings fields with the concrete settings-model fields and their types for every environment-dependent item.
What are the exact environment-variable names, settings-field names and field types for every listed item, and how does each variable map to its field?

quotes:
Registry's code receives each item as a field of the settings the one
   module that reads the environment loads; no other part of Registry reads
   a variable.
judgement.why: P1 already assigns the exact environment-variable names and their configuration encoding to State 6; the added requests for settings-field names, types and mappings are the same configuration-schema question.

precedent.topic: Exact case-sensitive environment-variable names and accepted aliases or service-name conversion
quotes:
The items are exactly these: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four
precedent.why: The exact case-sensitive environment-variable names and service-name encoding are configuration-contract and format details owned by State 6, while State 2 specifies the required items and their startup behavior.

topics.topic: Text-to-byte representation and validity rules for secret length and equality checks
questions: In which byte representation is the length of a secret received from a textual environment variable measured?
How is an environment/settings value converted to bytes for the 32-byte test, and are undecodable or non-canonical values malformed?
How is an environment-variable text value converted to the byte sequence whose length and equality are checked?

quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start. Registry checks the
   length and, by rule 4, the distinctness, and nothing else of how the owner
   made it (R0-23).
judgement.why: The quoted secret-length rule is unchanged in the closed and current A17 texts, and the reopening change about undeclared environment-variable names did not create or alter the byte-representation question.

topics.topic: Whether an empty service-token environment variable counts as set
questions: Does an environment variable that exists with an empty value count as a token being set for the all-or-none check, or as an unset token?

quotes:
the service tokens all four
   or none — none makes an owner-only start, and some but not all fail on the
   first missing one in rule 1's order
judgement.why: The quoted all-or-none rule is unchanged in the closed and current A17 texts, and the reopening change concerning names that designate no item did not alter whether an empty value counts as set.

topics.topic: Which identifier diagnostics use to name a failed configuration item
questions: What exact identifier must a diagnostic use to name an item: its environment-variable name, its settings-field name, or a human-readable label?

quotes:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).
judgement.why: State 2 fixes which failed item the diagnostic identifies and that it never contains the value, while the exact textual identifier and diagnostic format belong to State 6 contracts and formats.
